narrative.overview: The site is the sign a machinist already trusts: a safety-yellow field, ink-black header bands, white message panels, and a concrete ground, with one NOTICE blue reserved for Fleet and notices. Condensed uppercase signal words sit over a plain Barlow message face; the hazard stripe marks page seams.
keyCharacteristics: Yellow, ink, white, concrete base; one blue for a single meaning
Condensed uppercase signal words over humanist sans messages
3px ink edges and square panels; small radii only on controls and tags
Hazard stripe as the only ornamental pattern
Pictograms boxed in 3px black on yellow

rules.name: The One Notice Rule
rules.body: Blue means Fleet or informational notice. Do not use it as a general accent or decoration; yellow carries emphasis.

rules.name: The Ink-On-Yellow Rule
rules.body: Text on yellow is ink, text on ink is yellow or white, text on blue is white. Yellow is never a text color on white or concrete.

rules.name: The Signal Word Rule
rules.body: Barlow Condensed is only for short signal words, always uppercase. Sentences are always Barlow.

rules.name: The Message Weight Rule
rules.body: Weight 600 in Barlow marks the key term in a row; secondary lines are 400 in graphite.

rules.name: The Flat Sign Rule
rules.body: Panels, banners, tables, and callouts get a border, never a shadow. Only the button and the tag may cast one.

dos: Do build new content as a sign: ink banner with yellow caps heading over a white panel with a 3px ink edge.
Do keep text pairings to ink on yellow, yellow or white on ink, white on blue.
Do reserve NOTICE blue for Fleet and notices, and keep focus rings visible (3px, offset 3px).
Do use inline SVG pictograms boxed in 3px ink.
Do keep controls at 56px or taller on touch screens and respect reduced-motion.
donts: Don't use a dark-navy hero with a blue button, or a grid of rounded feature cards.
Don't set sentences or paragraphs in Barlow Condensed or in caps.
Don't add shadows to panels, banners, or tables.
Don't use yellow as text on white or concrete.
Don't repeat the hazard stripe inside content; it marks page seams only.
